claim: cppcheck containerOutOfBounds: tests/selftest.cpp:1599 moves[rng()%moves.size()] may index an empty vector
rationale: Not reachable. tests/selftest.cpp:1592-1598 is a closed guard chain: if moves.empty() the block either continues (drawFromStock() succeeded) or breaks (if (moves.empty()) break;). The only fall-through to line 1599 has moves non-empty. cppcheck cannot follow the two-exit guard.

claim: cppcheck knownConditionTrueFalse x3 in tests/uitest.cpp (327 whileDeactivated==0 always true; 467 r-step<0 always true; 3116 flightsInTheAir()==0 always false)
rationale: All three are cppcheck purity/value-flow assumptions that the source contradicts. 327: counter.count is mutated from a Qt event filter cppcheck does not model. 467: kRows=7 and step is 1..2 (uitest.cpp:417-418), so r-step is >=0 for r>=2 — cppcheck truncated the branch analysis (it emitted normalCheckLevelMaxBranches on this file). 3116: flightsInTheAir() changes as the view's QTimer runs during pump(3000); cppcheck treats the accessor as pure and carries the !=0 fact from line 3105.

claim: clazy lambda-in-connect x27 and connect-3arg-lambda x1 at src/canasta/canastaview.cpp:375-404 — captured local variable by reference might go out of scope before the lambda is called
rationale: The receiver cannot outlive the captures. src/canasta/canastaview.cpp:277 declares QDialog dlg on the stack; buttons and every spin/check widget are its children, and the connection is made to buttons->button(RestoreDefaults). The dialog is run modally at line 407 (dlg.exec()) and destroyed when the enclosing function returns, tearing the connection down with it, so the lambda cannot fire after handSize/canastaSize/... die. Same scope, same frame.

claim: ruff S602 and bandit B602: subprocess call with shell=True is a security issue at scripts/legibility-check.py:223
rationale: No untrusted input reaches the shell. THRESHOLD_GREP (scripts/legibility-check.py:213-219) is a module-level constant string literal with no interpolation, no f-string and no argv/env substitution; cwd=ROOT is a Path derived from __file__. There is no injection surface, so the finding cannot be reproduced as a defect. Kept flagged as style rather than fixed: the pipeline of three greps is what shell=True is for here.

claim: ruff B905: zip() without an explicit strict= parameter at scripts/scorepad-check.py:107 could silently truncate
rationale: Length-guarded three lines above. scripts/scorepad-check.py:103-105 tests len(want) != len(js) and records a problem; the zip at 107 sits in the else branch, so the two sequences are already known to be the same length. Truncation is unreachable, and the mismatch the check exists to catch is reported by the guard rather than swallowed by the zip.

claim: typos: `fpt` should be `ftp` at tests/uitest.cpp:940 (two hits)
rationale: Not a word. Line 940 is the printf format string "to %.2fpt against %.2fpt normal\n" — the token straddles the end of the %.2f conversion and the literal "pt" (points, the font unit). typos tokenises across the format specifier boundary. Both hits are the same construct.

claim: pyright: "LANCZOS" is not a known attribute of module "PIL.Image" at tools/make_scorepad_icon.py:60
rationale: Stub gap, not a runtime error. The installed Pillow is 12.3.0 and `from PIL import Image; Image.LANCZOS` evaluates to 1 — the module-level aliases were restored in Pillow 10 and are still present. pyright's bundled stubs only expose Image.Resampling.LANCZOS. The script runs; nothing to fix beyond a spelling preference.

claim: ruff S311: standard pseudo-random generators are not suitable for cryptographic purposes, tools/make_sounds.py:66
rationale: Deliberate and required. tools/make_sounds.py synthesises the 17 sound effects from a FIXED seed so re-running it is byte-identical — CLAUDE.md § Traps ("Sounds are generated, never sampled") records that as a licensing decision. A cryptographic RNG would break reproducibility, which is the property the script exists to have. No security context: nothing here keys, signs or authenticates.

claim: cppcheck uninitMemberVarNoCtor x8: Plate::score/hand/ours, Snapshot::toMove (draughts and reversi), Move::ai/bi/king have no initialiser
rationale: Every one of these aggregates is only ever brace-initialised at its single construction site, so no path reads an uninitialised member. src/canasta/canastaview.cpp:2524 `const Plate plates[2] = {...}`; src/draughts/draughtsview.cpp:409 `m_history.push_back({ m_board, m_toMove })` (read back only at :106); src/reversi/reversiview.cpp:418 `m_history.push_back({ m_board, m_toMove, m_lastMove })` (read at :143); tests/selftest.cpp:1573,1581 `moves.push_back({...})` filling all five fields. Latent hardening at best, no reproducible defect.
